name: Stourhead House

dates.altered: Library and picture gallery pavilions added 1796-1800 for Colt Hoare; east portico added 1840, from Campbell's C18 design; central block rebuilt 1902-06 by Doran Webb and Sir Aston Webb following the 1902 fire; balustraded parapets with ball finials added c1904.
dates.note: The list entry says '1721-24 for Henry Hoare by Colen Campbell'. The Wikipedia infobox says 'House: 1721-1724, destroyed in fire, rebuilt 1906'. They agree on the build and differ only in how much weight they give the rebuilding.

quotes.text: STOURTON WITH GASPER STOURHEAD PARK ST 73 SE (south side) 6/156 Stourhead House 6.1.66 GV I Country house. 1721-24 for Henry Hoare by Colen Campbell, library and picture gallery pavilions added 1796-1800 for Colt Hoare, east portico added 1840, 1902-06 rebuilding of central block by Doran Webb and Sir Aston Webb, following 1902 fire.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1131104, Details, header and opening sentence

quotes.text: Limestone ashlar, Lakeland slate hipped roofs, ashlar stacks. Central C18 range with added wings and pavilions, service court on north side. Two-storey over basements, 5-window.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1131104, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: Tetrastyle portico added 1840, from Campbell's C18 design, Composite columns to modillioned cornice and pediment with lead statue, from the Temple of Apollo (q.v.), chamfered rusticated basement with 6-pane sashes, balustraded steps up to portico flanked by large urns on plinths.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1131104, Details, east front

quotes.text: Principal floor has double half-glazed doors flanked by cross windows within portico, casement with pediment either side. First floor has 3 blind windows in moulded architraves with 2-light casement in eared and shouldered architrave either side, modillioned cornice to balustraded parapet with corner urns, attic block above pediment also with statues from Temple of Apollo.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1131104, Details, east front

quotes.text: Right and left returns of main block of ten bays; principal floors have Venetian windows and cross windows, all in Gibbs surrounds, first floors have ten cross windows in moulded architraves, good lead rainwater heads dated 1722.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1131104, Details, returns of the main block

measurements.name: portico_column_count
measurements.note: A READING: tetrastyle is four columns. The portico is an 1840 addition made from Campbell's own eighteenth-century design, so it is Campbell's intention executed a century late -- worth stating because a measurement of it is not a measurement of the 1721-24 house.

note: Tranche 3, English Baroque / Palladian / Adam cluster, 5 Sep 2026. Added as the plain, well-documented Palladian block: five windows by ten bays over a rusticated basement, two storeys, hipped Lakeland slate. It is `documentary` rather than `canonical` because the entry itself says the central block was rebuilt 1902-06 after a fire, so the fabric a surveyor measures today is Edwardian over a Campbell plan, and the portico that reads as the building's face was put up in 1840. Historic England serves the Details section hard-wrapped. Every run of whitespace in these quotes is the extractor's line wrap collapsed to one space; nothing else was changed, and a word broken across a wrap is left broken. No rights line for the list entry TEXT was read verbatim here, so no `rights_evidence` is recorded rather than a borrowed one.
